thread:
maya: Quick sync — we need to pick a scope for the 'Edge Connector' work that customers can deploy in their VPC/on‑prem to route traffic through customer-managed networking. three candidate scopes: Minimal, Medium, Full. Which should we target for Q2?
liam: TL;DR: medium. Minimal solves basics but won't cover rolling upgrades or complex NAT setups. Full is nice but slips timeline.
sophia: Agree with liam. Medium gives us punch-through + health checks + TLS termination. Keeps packaging work reasonable.
kevin: From docs POV: whatever we pick, we need clear upgrade/rollback instructions and a small quickstart. customers will want one-liner install and an offline package for airgap.
anita: Sales: two pilots (FinSys & MedCorp) are on hold until we have customer-routing + canary upgrade story. They'd pick medium if it guarantees zero-downtime upgrades.
liam: Zero-downtime is the hard part. We need: version pinning on agent, side‑by‑side deployment model (old+new), health endpoint, and traffic mirroring for canary.
sophia: Implementation notes: packaging should support both container and systemd installs. we'll provide a container image and an installer that drops systemd units for non-container customers. Also need to validate kernel and libc versions for our runtime.
maya: Good — propose we officialize Medium as the Q2 target: features = connector binary, TLS + mTLS config, NAT traversal guide, health checks, canary traffic routing, offline installer. Launch criteria: 1) install in >2 distros (ubuntu20/22 + rhel8), 2) canary upgrade verified on internal infra, 3) docs, 4) security review.
liam: Add: automatic rollback on >X% error rate and audit log for connections. Also requirement: control plane must not exfiltrate customer tokens (double-check KMS local mode).
sophia: For upgrades let's add a simple API: /v1/connector/health and /v1/connector/ready plus a migration tool that copies KV caches between versions. That covers stateful models with KV caches.
kevin: I'll draft the quickstart and troubleshooting appendix. Need example firewall rules and sample systemd.
kevin: sample firewall snippet for GCP ingress: 
``
# allow egress to our control plane endpoints
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.82.12.45 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
```
kevin: systemd sample we can include: 
``
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Edge Connector
After=network.target
[Service]
ExecStart=/opt/redwood/bin/edge_connector --config /etc/redwood/connector.yaml
Restart=on-failure
```
anita: Can we add a checkbox for FIPS/HSM requirements? MedCorp flagged that explicitly. Even if we don't ship FIPS in Medium, we should list it in roadmap as 'enterprise add-on'.
maya: Yes — add to enterprise add-ons: FIPS build, HSM/KMS integration, airgap CA rotation tool. Not blockers for Medium.
liam: Ops ask: we need a health test harness so SREs can simulate multi‑version traffic. I'll spin up a small test repo with harness that runs canary against real models.
sophia: Note: runtime changes minimal if connector only handles network + caching. But packaging must bundle compatible quantized model variants for offline installs (customers expect models to come in package). That increases artifact size.
maya: Decision: Medium scope accepted for Q2. Owners: sophia (eng lead), liam (sre lead), kevin (docs), maya (product). Deliverables and dates: RFC by 1845060000 (end of week), Installer alpha 1845500000 (early May), internal canary 1846000000 (mid May), pilot with FinSys 1847000000 (June).
deploy-bot: RFC rfc-546-edge-connector draft uploaded by maya — https://internal/redwood/rfcs/546
kevin: Action items for docs: quickstart + offline package guide + upgrade playbook. I'll front-load quickstart for alpha.
sophia: Action items for eng: create installer, CI for offline bundles, health endpoints, canary mirroring. I'll open tickets and link in RFC.
liam: Action items for SRE: test harness + rollback automation + run pilot. I'll create the test repo and invite kevin for docs integration.
maya: Risk log: 1) offline package size -> mitigation: delta patching and compressed models, 2) airgap cert rotation complexity -> mitigation: CA rotation tool and clear operational docs, 3) upgrade rollback complexity -> mitigation: traffic mirroring + automated rollback.
anita: I'll update pilot asks to emphasize canary and compliance needs.
maya: OK — thanks everyone. will convert this thread into RFC comments and tag owners. If no blockers, we'll proceed with Medium. :thumbsup:
